# cohesity Provider



## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "cohesity" {
  cluster_vip      = "0.0.0.0"
  cluster_username = "cohesity"
  cluster_password = "cohesity"
  cluster_domain   = "LOCAL"
  support_password = "cohesity"
}
```

## Authentication

Existing resources require `cluster_vip`, `cluster_username` and
`cluster_password` (or the corresponding `COHESITY_IP`, `COHESITY_USERNAME` and
`COHESITY_PASSWORD` environment variables).

For `cohesity_web_server_certificate`, use an `api_key` with `CLUSTER_VIEW` and
`CLUSTER_MODIFY`, supplied directly or through `COHESITY_API_KEY`. Set `endpoint`
to the cluster HTTPS origin, or supply `cluster_vip`. API-key-only configuration
is supported for certificate management; other resources retain their existing
username/password authentication.

`ca_certificate_pem` extends system trust for certificate management.
`bootstrap_certificate_pem` optionally pins verified current server leaves when
replacing an initial self-signed certificate. Normal CA validation remains
available during rotation. Write-only certificate keys require Terraform 1.11+.

## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) API key with CLUSTER_VIEW and CLUSTER_MODIFY for web server certificate management. Defaults to COHESITY_API_KEY. Other resources require username/password authentication.
- `bootstrap_certificate_pem` (String) PEM bundle of explicitly verified existing server leaves, accepted only when normal CA validation fails.
- `ca_certificate_pem` (String) Additional trusted CA certificates for certificate management.

- `cluster_domain` (String) The domain name of cohesity user
- `cluster_password` (String, Sensitive) Cohesity cluster password
- `cluster_username` (String) Cohesity cluster username
- `cluster_vip` (String) IP or hostname of Cohesity cluster node
- `endpoint` (String) HTTPS origin for certificate management. Defaults to https://cluster_vip.
- `support_password` (String, Sensitive) support password for the Cohesity cluster
